newsitem.title: GERMANY: German new crop wheat steadier on buying interest.
newsitem.headline: German new crop wheat steadier on buying interest.

text.p: German wheat prices have steadied as buyers are beginning to show interest in new crop volumes, brokers said.
Nominal German fob levels were raised as a result of weather fears in France last week which raised quality concerns and spoiled some of the French business in southern Europe to Germany's benefit.
But brokers said it was arguable whether sellers could maintain the higher levels in future trades as French prices were slipping.
"July/August markets will be ruled by the weather in France," one said.
Concern British and French crops may be late and show some yield reductions as a result of excessive rainfall may support German prices.
The Hamburg grain exchange left its spot bread wheat price (12.5 percent protein, 220 hagberg) unchanged from last week's 265 marks a tonne.
The spot feed wheat price was raised by 2.50 marks to 262.50, with old crop hardly available and British supplies uncompetitive due to the strong pound.
Farmers were getting ready to start the barley harvest in the south and the east of Germany.
New crop rye sellers reduced levels to attract business.
Fob Baltic sellers put July delivery wheat at 270-280 marks (12 percent) and material with 13/14 percent protein at 280-320 marks. Old crop rye was at 265 marks.
New crop September wheat is now in a 270-310 marks range, depending on quality, up 2.50-5.00 on the week.
New crop rye (July/Aug) indications have been dropped by 7.50 marks to 242.50-247.50 and new crop barley is indicated at 235 marks after fob Baltic trades at 230-234.
